claim: Retinal glasses or contacts are routinely used
originalWording: Retinal glasses or contacts are routinely used

sources.title: The Age of Spiritual Machines — Ray Kurzweil (1999)
sources.locator: Computers and communications in 2019: direct-eye displays

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: People routinely wear direct retinal-projection eyeglasses or contact lenses delivering resolution higher than normal human vision.
strict.rationale: Routine everyday retinal glasses or contact lenses with above-human visual acuity did not exist in 2019 and still do not exist in 2026. Bulky VR gaming headsets like Oculus Quest fail the form-factor, retinal-projection, routine-wear, and acuity bars simultaneously.
changedConditions: Enforces routine wearing, direct retinal projection, and above-human acuity

evidence.title: Microvision: Nomad retinal display installed at Chevrolet dealership
evidence.note: Microvision-issued release hosted by The Auto Channel: actual industrial deployment. Head-worn see-through retinal display; not ordinary prescription-glasses styling or mass consumer adoption.

evidence.title: Qualcomm: Snapdragon platform powers shipping Oculus Quest
evidence.note: Primary institutional, research, or issuer source. Dates in the claim refer to the observation or product event, not the review date.

reference.criterion: Retinal glasses/contacts with the specified exceptional resolution are routinely worn, not just demonstrated.
reference.rationale: Near-eye displays existed in 2019, but mainstream routine use at the asserted acuity did not. Practical headsets/AR prove part of the direction, not routine retinal contacts or acuity above human vision.

broader.criterion: Consumer near-eye VR/AR headsets achieve practical commercial availability, falling short of routine everyday retinal eyewear.
broader.rationale: Standalone headsets such as Oculus Quest (2019) proved consumer near-eye displays are commercially viable, earning partial credit. Treating enclosed gaming headsets as full on-time fulfillment of routine above-human-acuity retinal glasses/contacts stretches the claim past recognition.
changedConditions: Credits consumer VR/AR headsets as partial without treating them as routine retinal glasses/contacts
